lesson_title: Fuel That Falls From the Sky
hook_text: Imagine a filling station where the petrol is free, forever. South Africa owns one of the best on earth — and barely uses it.
clip_script: Picture a filling station where the fuel is free — forever. You pay to build the pumps, and then the fuel just arrives, every day, no charge. That is the entire logic of solar and wind: sunshine and wind cost nothing; only the catching machines cost money. Coal has to be mined, railed and burned every day it works. A solar panel is paid for once and harvests free fuel for twenty-five years. And here is the almost unfair part: South Africa's sky pours out more of this free fuel than nearly anywhere on the planet. The Northern Cape gets over 2 500 hours of sunshine a year — world-premium sun — while two oceans drive steady wind onto our coasts. Germany, under its permanent grey blanket, built a world-leading solar industry with HALF our sunshine. Now meet the machines. The PV panel: sunlight straight to electricity, no moving parts — a silent windowpane, from your neighbour's roof to the mega-farms of Upington. The CSP plant: thousands of mirrors playing the magnifying-glass trick on one glowing tower, cooking molten salt that holds its heat like a giant thermos — Redstone near Postmasburg stores TWELVE HOURS of it, making supper-time electricity from lunchtime sun. The wind turbine: a skyscraper pinwheel where doubling the wind gives EIGHT times the power. The auctions have already spoken: new sun and wind are now cheaper than new coal. The fuel is free, the fuel is ours — the race is only about building the pumps.
visual_style: A dreamlike petrol station where sunbeams and wind stream into the pumps; a sunshine-hours map glowing over the Northern Cape against a grey Germany; the three machines animating in sequence — windowpane panel, mirror field igniting a tower, turbine towering over grazing sheep; a falling price graph crossing below coal.
mood: Optimistic, almost incredulous at the free lunch, ending urgent.
pacing: Bright quick open, wonder-slow on the mirror field and thermos, punchy acceleration through the cube law to the price-crossing finale.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and weigh the whole energy future — machines, obstacles and all.
